text: Last lesson of this chapter: modules — how Python code gets organized and reused, and how you bring in libraries other people wrote.
A module is just a .py file of code you can reuse by importing it. Python ships with a huge standard library for free — json, os, datetime — no installation needed.
A few import forms: import json, use it as json.loads. from json import loads, use loads directly with no prefix. Prefer the first for several things, the second for just one or two names.
The standard library ships with Python itself. Third-party packages — requests, openai, pandas — don't; you install them separately with pip. Once installed, you import them the same way.
Any .py file you write is itself a module other files can import. This is how real projects stay organized — and it's exactly the mechanism every AI provider's SDK uses: pip install, then import.
That closes out Chapter 1. Chapter 2 moves into the data structures you'll use constantly to shape data for an AI API, starting with lists and comprehensions.
